This pattern is consistent with Recurrent Depressive Disorder , which is characterised by two or more depressive episodes with a minimum of 2 months between episodes. Depression (single episode) (Option A) refers to a single occurrence of a major depressive episode without any prior history.

Balanced salt solution plus glutathione contains bicarbonate, glucose, and glutathione, which help maintain endothelial pump function, reduce oxidative stress, and preserve corneal clarity during phaco. Hence, it is the best irrigating fluid.

gold.primary: Selection of intraocular irrigating solution for phacoemulsification

items.explanation: Hyperthermia Correct Answer: B) Hyperthermia Explanation: Myxedema coma is the life-threatening extreme of hypothyroidism and carries a 20-40% mortality rate , even with intensive treatment. Importantly, clinical outcomes are independent of serum T4 and TSH levels. Clinical manifestations include: Reduced level of consciousness ranging from confusion → somnolence → coma Seizures and other abnormal CNS signs Profound hypothermia (may reach 23°C) Hypoventilation leading to hypercapnia (Option D) and hypoxemia Severe hypothyroidism → ↓ respiratory drive + muscle weakness → CO₂ retention (respiratory acidosis).

items.subject: Pathology
items.stem: A 45-year-old patient visits a haematologist with symptoms of weakness and fatigue. Laboratory tests show low haemoglobin, a low reticulocyte count, and normal WBC and platelet counts. The bone marrow analysis reveals a selective reduction in erythroid precursors. What is the likely diagnosis?
items.options: {'html': 'Aplasti\u200dc anemia', 'is_correct': False, 'key': 'A'} | {'html': 'Pure red c\u200dell aplasia', 'is_correct': True, 'key': 'B'} | {'html': 'Iron defici\u200dency anaemia', 'is_correct': False, 'key': 'C'} | {'html': 'Pernicio\u200dus anemia', 'is_correct': False, 'key': 'D'}
items.explanation: Pure red cell aplasia Correct Answer: B) Pure red cell aplasia Explanation: The scenario of weakness, fatigue, low haemoglobin, low reticulocyte count, normal WBC and platelet counts, and bone marrow showing a selective reduction in erythroid precursors is consistent with Pure Red Cell Alasia (PRCA) , which is characterized by a marked reduction or absence of red blood cell precursors while other hematopoietic cell lines remain normal. It is a primary marrow disorder in which only erythroid progenitors are suppressed (red cell progenitors are completely absent in severe cases). Causes: Associated with neoplasms (thymoma and large granular lymphocytic leukaemia) Drug exposures Autoimmune disorders Parvovirus infection Clinical features: Fatigue, weakness, pallor, frequent infections, easy bruising or bleeding, and shortness of breath due to insufficient production of red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets.

gold.primary: Diagnosis of pure red cell aplasia

items.subject: Pharmacology
items.stem: Diuretics possessing the highest natriuretic efficacy, often referred to as high-ceiling diuretics, primarily exert their action on which anatomical segment of the nephron?
items.options: {'html': 'Proximal convoluted tubule\u200c', 'is_correct': False, 'key': 'A'} | {'html': 'Thick ascending limb of th\u200ce loop of Henle', 'is_correct': True, 'key': 'B'} | {'html': 'Distal convo\u200cluted tubule', 'is_correct': False, 'key': 'C'} | {'html': 'Cortical col\u200clecting duct', 'is_correct': False, 'key': 'D'}
items.correct_answer: B. Thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle
items.explanation: Thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle Correct Answer: B) Thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle Explanation: The thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle is the site where approximately 25% of the filtered sodium load is reabsorbed via the Na + -K + -2Cl − symporter. Diuretics acting here, known as loop diuretics or high-ceiling agents , disrupt the kidney's ability to concentrate urine by abolishing the corticomedullary osmotic gradient. This segment has a massive capacity for salt reabsorption that cannot be fully compensated for by downstream segments; inhibitors of this site produce the most profound diuresis and natriuresis compared to all other diuretic classes.

gold.primary: Nephron site of action of loop diuretics

Saliva and urine samples are more sensitive than blood because not all infants with congenital CMV are viremic at birth.

This is a classical case of vesico-vaginal fistula. Vesico-vaginal fistula (VVF): Vesico-vaginal fistula (VVF) is an abnormal passage that develops between the bladder and the vagina, leading to continuous and involuntary discharge of urine through the vagina.

She describes a dark vertical line running down her abdomen, dark patches on her face, and pinkish lines on her thighs. She denies any itching, pain, or other systemic symptoms. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she is not on any medications apart from prenatal vitamins. What is the most likely explanation for these skin changes?

items.explanation: Linea Nigra, Chloasma (Melasma), and Striae Gravidarum Correct Answer: A) Linea Nigra, Chloasma (Melasma), and Striae Gravidarum Explanation: During pregnancy, various physiological skin changes can occur due to hormonal influences: Linea Nigra : A dark vertical line running down the abdomen due to increased melanocyte-stimulating hormone. Chloasma (Melasma) : Hyperpigmented patches on the face, often called the "mask of pregnancy," due to hormonal changes and sometimes exacerbated by sun exposure. Striae Gravidarum : Pinkish or purplish lines, commonly known as stretch marks, which appear on the abdomen, thighs, or breasts due to the stretching of the skin.

The counter-current multiplier specifically refers to the mechanisms occurring within the loop of Henle and associated structures in the medulla, not the cortical regions.

Innate immunity provides immediate, non-specific defense against pathogens and does not require prior exposure . It includes physical barriers, phagocytic cells, natural killer cells, complement, antimicrobial peptides, and certain innate-like lymphocytes.

items.stem: During pregnancy there is increased demand for calcium, as the fetus requires about 30 g of calcium for skeletal development. Which of the following maternal physiological changes helps meet this increased calcium requirement?

items.correct_answer: D. Enhanced intestinal calcium absorption due to increased calcitriol levels
items.explanation: Enhanced intestinal calcium absorption due to increased calcitriol levels Correct Answer: D) Enhanced intestinal calcium absorption due to increased calcitriol levels Explanation: Fetal skeletal growth, especially in the third trimester, demands a large increase in maternal calcium supply. To meet this need, pregnancy induces a rise in calcitriol (1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D) levels. Calcitriol significantly increases intestinal absorption of calcium from the maternal diet.

items.stem: A blunt force injury produces a laceration with characteristic radiating skin tears at both ends. What is this appearance called?
items.options: {'html': 'Sparrow\u200d’s foot', 'is_correct': False, 'key': 'A'} | {'html': 'Wed\u200dging', 'is_correct': False, 'key': 'B'} | {'html': 'Fish t\u200dailing', 'is_correct': False, 'key': 'C'} | {'html': 'Swallow\u200d tailing', 'is_correct': True, 'key': 'D'}
items.explanation: Swallow tailing Correct Answer: D) Swallow tailing Explanation: Swallow tailing occurs when a blunt object (like a car bumper) strikes the skin at an angle. The force "undermines" the skin and tears it in two directions at the end, resembling the tail of a swallow. Sparrow’s foot (Option A): It is a characteristic, small, V-shaped laceration on the face or limbs caused by shattering tempered glass, typically from a car windshield during a road accident, resembling bird tracks.

gold.primary: Recognition of swallow-tailing in blunt-force lacerations

items.stem: A patient with acute hepatitis is HBsAg positive with anti-HDV antibodies. To represent HDV superinfection on chronic hepatitis B rather than HBV-HDV coinfection. Which antibody profile confirms HDV superinfection?
items.options: {'html': 'IgM anti-H\u200bBc positive', 'is_correct': False, 'key': 'A'} | {'html': 'IgG anti-H\u200bBc positive', 'is_correct': True, 'key': 'B'} | {'html': 'Anti-HBs\u200b positive', 'is_correct': False, 'key': 'C'} | {'html': 'IgM anti-H\u200bAV positive', 'is_correct': False, 'key': 'D'}
items.explanation: IgG anti-HBc positive Correct Answer: B) IgG anti-HBc positive Explanation: IgG anti-HBc indicates chronic hepatitis B infection; when HDV infection occurs on this background, it confirms HDV superinfection, not coinfection. Key serologic principle in hepatitis differentiation: HBsAg indicates active HBV infection IgM anti-HBc → acute HBV infection IgG anti-HBc → chronic HBV infection HDV requires HBV (HBsAg) for replication HDV infection patterns: Coinfection: Acute HBV + acute HDV → IgM anti-HBc positive Superinfection: Chronic HBV + acute HDV → IgG anti-HBc positive Superinfection is associated with more severe disease and a higher risk of chronic liver failure. IgM anti-HBc (Option A): Indicates acute HBV, consistent with coinfection, not superinfection.

gold.primary: Serologic distinction of HDV superinfection from coinfection

items.stem: Which vaccine among the options exhibits a seroconversion rate that is quicker than the incubation period of the corresponding disease?
items.options: {'html': 'Coron\u200cavirus', 'is_correct': False, 'key': 'A'} | {'html': 'Mea\u200csles', 'is_correct': True, 'key': 'B'} | {'html': 'Po\u200clio', 'is_correct': False, 'key': 'C'} | {'html': 'Mu\u200cmps', 'is_correct': False, 'key': 'D'}
items.explanation: Measles Correct Answer: B) Measles Amongst the above options, measles vaccine has a faster seroconversion rate as compared to the incubation period of the disease and this is why measles vaccine is given when a disaster or an epidemic occurs. Seroconversion: is the transition from the point of viral infection to when antibodies of the virus become present in the blood. Seroconversion rates are one of the methods used for determining the efficacy of a vaccine.

gold.primary: Rapid measles-vaccine seroconversion relative to disease incubation

items.stem: Which of the following genes, encoding an X-linked inhibitor of apoptosis, has been identified as a cause of monogenic very-early-onset inflammatory bowel disease (VEOIBD)?
items.options: {'html': 'NO\u200cD2', 'is_correct': False, 'key': 'A'} | {'html': 'XI\u200cAP', 'is_correct': True, 'key': 'B'} | {'html': 'ATG\u200c16L1', 'is_correct': False, 'key': 'C'} | {'html': 'LR\u200cRK2', 'is_correct': False, 'key': 'D'}
items.explanation: XIAP Correct Answer: B) XIAP Explanation: XIAP (X-linked inhibitor of apoptosis protein) mutations cause monogenic VEOIBD , typically presenting in infancy or early childhood with severe, refractory intestinal inflammation. Loss of XIAP disrupts immune regulation and apoptosis, leading to uncontrolled intestinal immune activation. VEOIBD (<6 years) often reflects single-gene (monogenic) immune defects, unlike adolescent/adult IBD.

gold.primary: XIAP mutation in monogenic very-early-onset IBD
